 Live .  14,701 viewing 14701 viewing England fall to 150-6 as they seek big finish v Australia in first T20
 Sat 21 Nov 2026 , Men's International Twenty20 Match - 1st T20I Australia vs England (batting), in play Australia Australia In Play England England Yet to bat 158 -6 ( 16.4 ) England are 158 for 6 with 3.2 overs remaining Australia: yet to bat England innings: 158 for 6 from 16.4 overs, in play

 by Matthew Henry
 Eng 155-6 published at 16 overs 16 overs 
 Cox 11, Dawson 4 
 England have sent in Liam Dawson rather than Jamie Overton, which may be because they want to keep Overton away from the spin. 
 Chaudhary, born in Delhi and playing his fouth match for Australia, has been really impressive. 
 He ends with 2-21 from four overs.

 Darren Lehmann 
Ex-Australia coach on Test Match Special 
 Fantastic catch from Lachlan Shaw - it's never easy at the MCG and Australia have dropped a few tonight.
 A great time for a wicket for Australia.
 7 44 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 WICKET published at 15.1 overs 15.1 overs 
 Curran c Shaw b Chaudhary 21 (Eng 150-6) 
 Spinner Nikhil Chaudhary strikes again! Sam Curran had done the work to get himself in but skews a drive straight to deep cover when looking to kick on. 
 Australia are still fighting just about.
 15 121 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 150-5 published at 15 overs 15 overs 
 England have already gone beyond the 138 they needed to beat Pakistan in the T20 World Cup final on this ground in 2022. 
 It's a tricky pitch to judge. Harry Brook made it look like the Hume Highway to Sydney but most of the rest have found it tricky. 
 Jordan Cox flicks one fine to get his first boundary. 
 34 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing

 Sam Curran places the ball really well. England will be looking at around 200 or 210.

 Eng 141-5 published at 14 overs 14 overs 
 Curran 17, Cox 5 
 Sam Curran ends a run of four overs without a boundary by drilling Adam Zampa straight. Curran and Jordan Cox are pushing hard, trying to pick up the twos, but Australia have remembered how to hold onto the ball.

 That record felt in danger when Brook and Banton were flying. The international record - 186-5 by India against Zimbabwe at the 2022 World Cup - is still under threat. 
 Sam Curran is a man under pressure after a quiet run in the ODIs.
